**WattBridge- Senior Director, Information Technology**

**About WattBridge**

The global energy landscape is rapidly changing, and we're here to accelerate that change. From the decommissioning of high-carbon power assets, accelerated expansion of renewable energy resources as baseload power, to the advent of the prosumer. The volatility on today's energy grid has never been greater. WattBridge was conceived by power industry experts to enable the sustained integration of highly efficient, reduced carbon dispatchable power generation assets on our national energy grid.

**Position Summary**

WattBridge, the world’s preeminent LM6000 delivery platform, is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology to develop, implement, and own the company’s information technology (IT), cybersecurity and data strategy that will support the origination, development and commercial operations of a full power delivery platform focused on data center campus style development. WattBridge developed, financed, built, owned and operated the world’s largest LM6000 portfolio consisting of 2400 MW’s from 2019 thru 2026. The platform raised over $2BN in capital and is now partnered with Energy Capital Partners as our majority sponsor. With competitive advantages in secured power equipment as an OEM, a proven track record in building out a 2400 MW portfolio, and a fully vertically integrated execution platform, we are well positioned to be highly successful in the data center industry.

The primary focus of this role is developing and leading the separation of IT and cybersecurity services from Parent Company under the Transition Services Agreement (TSA), stands up an independent, cloud-native technology platform within twelve months of close, and then runs that platform through a small internal team and a managed service model. The position builds enterprise-grade IT, cybersecurity, and governance from the outset, secures operational technology (OT) at the company's generation assets, and establishes the controls, reporting, and data foundation expected of a private equity-backed company preparing for future capital markets activity.

**Reports to**: Vice President Business Development.

**Work Location:** Remote United States

**Position Responsibilities**

* Serve as WattBridge's TSA workstream lead for IT and cybersecurity, coordinating with the PROENERGY counterpart and owning monthly service reviews
* Deliver the IT and cybersecurity exit milestones within the 12-month TSA term, including an independent Microsoft 365 tenant, a live MSP contract, and full endpoint migration
* Build and execute the 90-day transition plans required before each TSA exit, including knowledge transfer, data migration, and systems access cutover
* Enforce WattBridge data ownership and portability rights, ensuring all company data is extracted and validated before TSA systems access ends
* Track TSA service levels, cost-plus charges, and scope changes, escalating issues through the governance model defined in the agreement
* Define WattBridge's technology strategy and roadmap under the principle of outsourcing infrastructure while owning data and insights
* Select cloud-native, low-administration platforms that employee growth and beyond without re-platforming
* Partner with Finance, Commercial, Development, and HR leaders to select and deploy core business systems, including ERP, HRIS, project and pipeline management, and document management
* Embed AI capabilities from day one, including Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, a governed AI use-case pipeline, and an enterprise data and analytics foundation (Power BI)
* Plan the technology footprint for asset operations if O&M transitions from PROENERGY, including CMMS, asset performance monitoring, and predictive maintenance (AMPS / PI)
* Establish and lead the cybersecurity program, including policies, standards, risk management, identity and access management, and incident response
* Oversee the managed detection and response (MDR/SOC) partner, Microsoft Defender endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and the incident response retainer
* Secure OT/ICS environments at generation assets, including deployment of passive OT monitoring (Claroty or Dragos) and IT/OT segmentation
* Ensure compliance with NERC CIP and other applicable regulatory requirements for generation assets, and support audits and regulatory inspections
* Run security awareness training and phishing simulation for all employees and contractors
* Establish IT governance aligned with NIST CSF, including IT general controls (ITGCs) that support lender reporting, audit, and future SOX readiness
* Build and manage the IT and cybersecurity operating and capital budgets, including the one-time Day-1 infrastructure and end-user equipment plan
* Report technology risk, cybersecurity posture, and program status to the executive team, PE sponsor, and board as required
* Develop business continuity and disaster recovery capability, including backup (Azure Backup), recovery objectives, and tested recovery plans
* Lead competitive selection of a Houston-based managed service provider and define contract scope, service level agreements, and performance reporting
* Negotiate and manage all technology vendor, licensing, and telecommunications agreements for value and security compliance
* Hire, lead, and develop IT staff, setting goals, standards, and on-call expectations
* Deliver a consistent onboarding experience as the company scales through each hiring wave, from equipment and accounts on day one to security training

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field
* Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years in IT leadership roles

**Job Description**
-------------------

The NYC Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) enriches the environment and protects public health for all New Yorkers by providing 1.1 billion gallons of high-quality drinking water, managing wastewater and stormwater, and reducing air, noise, and hazardous materials pollution. DEP is the largest combined municipal and wastewater utility in the country, with nearly 6,000 employees. DEP's water supply system is comprised of 19 reservoirs and 3 controlled lakes throughout the system’s 2,000 square mile watershed that extends 125 miles north and west of the city.
  
  
The New York City Department of Environmental Protection (NYC DEP) Business Information Technology (BIT) division is responsible for providing quality business, technical, and information technology system support to agency users. This commitment is achieved through collaboration, strong relationships, and a unified vision with DEP partners to deliver technology solutions that support the agency’s operational needs. Providing these services ensures that DEP continues its tradition of delivering excellent service to the residents of New York City.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Information Officer (CIO), the Business Information Technology team seeks to hire a Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). Responsibilities include cybersecurity strategy, architecture, solutions design, program coordination and execution, awareness and outreach, business management, and reporting on the effectiveness of the information security program. This position requires a seasoned leader with strong business acumen and a detailed working knowledge of information security technologies, practices, and policies and their application in a business environment. The CISO will research and recommend innovative solutions and improvements to existing procedures. The CISO is an implementer who possesses the poise and ability to act calmly and competently in high-pressure situations. This role is responsible for developing and managing strong strategic relationships within Information Technology (IT) and ensuring that projects, initiatives, and security platforms meet all required security standards.
  
  
Under varying levels of executive direction, with latitude for independent initiative, judgment, and decision making, the selected candidate will develop and implement the organization’s information security strategy to protect data and systems from cyber threats. The CISO will safeguard information system assets by identifying security risks, threats, and vulnerabilities affecting networks, systems, and applications across new and existing technology initiatives, the selected candidate will evaluate high-level information technology initiatives and provide technical guidance to ensure compliance with security policies, standards, and guidelines. Responsibilities include developing, implementing, enforcing, and communicating security policies and plans covering data, software applications, hardware, and telecommunications systems.
  
  
The role requires in-depth knowledge of Internet Protocol (IP) networking and networking protocols, along with security technologies including encryption, Internet Protocol Security (IPsec), Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), firewalls, proxy services, Domain Name System (DNS), electronic mail systems, privileged access management, and access lists. Experience with Operational Technology (OT) networks and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) environments is also required.
  
  
The candidate will serve as a recognized subject matter expert in internet, web, application, and network security engineering, including vulnerability assessments, network scanning, and threat surface analysis. The role also requires advanced knowledge of cloud service security models and enterprise data protection strategies, including backup architecture, disaster recovery planning, and business continuity frameworks.
  
  
The candidate will oversee the system’s cybersecurity program and also support the new NYS Cybersecurity requirements for water and wastewater.
  
The candidate must have:
  

* Proven knowledge of core cybersecurity principles, including the ability to understand, interpret, and apply cybersecurity policies, standards, and regulatory requirements.
* Practical, hands-on experience in system protection or risk management, demonstrating the ability to identify security risks, evaluate vulnerabilities, and support incident response activities.
* Experience implementing or supporting cybersecurity programs in environments involving critical infrastructure, public utilities, operational technology (OT), or similar high-risk systems.
* The capability to serve as the responsible authority for developing, maintaining, and ensuring compliance with the system’s cybersecurity program.

  
  
Essential Job Functions:
  
  

* Lead the development, coordination, and submission of materials required to maintain compliance with the New York State Cybersecurity Regulations for Public Water Systems.

At Fullbay, our mission is simple — to create safer roads for our families and yours. **Position Overview:**

Fullbay's Security and IT Manager owns two functions that are usually split across two people: the security program that keeps Fullbay's systems, people, and customer data safe, and the IT operations that keep the business running day to day. Reporting to the VP of IT, this role designs the security and IT program from the ground up and owns its execution end-to-end — there's no existing playbook to inherit and no separate team to hand the work to.

This role is well-suited to someone who has built a security program before, not just operated inside one — someone comfortable being the primary responder when an MDR alert escalates, the person who leads SOC 2 through an actual audit, and the same person who's also the company's escalation point when someone's laptop won't image. A shop's most dangerous moments are never the ones people see coming. Production planners, customer service, sales reps, designers, marketers, and finance should each have AI woven into how they work, backed by systems they trust. Getting there is your job.

Fireclay Tile has always used technology to do things differently. We were early to the cloud, and over the last few years we have gone well past experimentation: we now run production AI skills, agents, and internal applications that our teams use every day.

We are a vertically integrated, employee-owned B Corp that makes beautiful, sustainable tile and helps clients carry a project from inspiration through installation. The work is real: complex product data, factories, supply chain, sales, design, customer service, showrooms, installation, finance, and thousands of decisions that need to happen well every day.

Owning AI here means owning more than tools. You will define and run the enterprise architecture, security, governance, and process controls that let AI scale safely across every team. That includes how models and agents access data, who can do what, how work is reviewed, how we audit and observe it, and how we decide what gets built, bought, scaled, or stopped.

This is not a role for an AI futurist who stays at 30,000 feet. You will be in the weeds: mapping work, finding constraints, building solutions, coaching teammates, and holding a high bar for security, quality, and measurable impact.

**How We Work**

We run our technology team like a software startup inside a manufacturing company. The pace is fast, the team is lean, and shipping matters more than planning decks.

In exchange, you get a lot of autonomy. You will have the room to learn the business deeply, decide where technology and AI can add value, and act on it quickly without waiting on layers of approval.

With AI, the distance between an idea and a working application is now days, not quarters. It is normal here to scope a problem with a business owner on Friday, build the application with AI over the weekend, and put it in front of real users on Monday. We want someone who finds that energizing, and who knows how to move that fast without cutting corners on security, data integrity, or review.

**Our Stack**

Claude, MCP, custom skills and agents, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Shopify Plus, Front, Dialpad, Slack, Hyros, HubSpot

**The Opportunities You'll Have**

* Own the AI rollout across every Fireclay team, from production and supply chain to customer service, marketing, sales, and finance.
* Partner with the VP of Technology and the CEO to define the next vision of Fireclay's technology, built on AI.
* Design and run the enterprise architecture for AI: how agents, skills, and applications connect to Salesforce, Google Cloud, Shopify, and Snowflake, and how data flows between them.
* Own AI security, governance, and process control: access and permissions, data privacy, human review, audit trails, observability, and clear ownership for every production workflow.
* Lead, mentor, and grow Fireclay's development team, and raise the bar for how we build.
* Learn Fireclay deeply, from customer journey and order flow through manufacturing, fulfillment, installation, and support, and find the real points of friction, delay, rework, and opportunity.
* Build and ship AI-enabled workflows and applications quickly, often in days, that improve productivity, decision quality, customer experience, revenue, or cost.
* Identify and pursue customer-facing AI opportunities that make it easier to discover, design, purchase, receive, and install Fireclay products.
* Run a disciplined intake and prioritization process. Every meaningful AI investment should have a defined problem, baseline, owner, cost, expected value, success metric, security review, and scale-or-stop decision.
* Make the right build-versus-buy decisions. Use external tools, partners, and emerging models where they create leverage, without creating a fragile or ungoverned stack.

**What Success Looks Like Early**

* First 30 days: Map Fireclay's stack across Salesforce, Google Cloud, Shopify, and Snowflake, along with current AI use, developer capacity, core data flows, security posture, and highest-friction business processes. Meet the people doing the work, including in the physical operation. Ship something small and useful.

The CTO owns technology strategy, architecture standards, AI-enabled engineering transformation, cybersecurity and platform-risk direction, technology investment priorities, and enterprise technical readiness. **Position Summary**

The SSVF Program Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for Veterans Bridge Home's Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, ensuring high-quality, veteran-centered services that prevent and end homelessness among veterans and their families. Reporting to the Market Executive Director, this position is responsible for the day-to-day management of the SSVF grant, including program operations, staff supervision, compliance, quality assurance, and community partnerships. The Program Manager will work directly with the Compliance department and Finance team. The Program Manager ensures services are delivered in accordance with Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations, Housing First principles, and Veterans Bridge Home policies while maintaining a strong focus on measurable outcomes and continuous improvement.

This position serves as the operational leader for the SSVF program by fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and innovation. Working closely with internal departments and community partners, the Program Manager develops strategies to improve housing stability, enhance program performance, strengthen partnerships, and ensure responsible stewardship of federal grant resources. The Program Manager contributes to Veterans Bridge Home's mission by connecting service members, veterans, and their families to the communities where they live and thrive. This is a grant-funded position.

Program Leadership

* Provide operational leadership for the Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with VA regulations (38 CFR Part 62), grant requirements, organizational policies, and a Housing First, veteran-centered approach.

* Direct coordinated outreach efforts to identify and engage eligible veterans who are experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness.

Grant Administration & Operations

* Oversee program intake, eligibility determinations, and referral processes to ensure timely, equitable, and consistent access to services.
* Ensure eligibility determinations meet SSVF requirements, including veteran status, household income at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI), and literally homeless or imminent-risk status under the “but for” standard.

* Oversee the appropriate, compliant, and timely use of Temporary Financial Assistance (TFA), including rental assistance, security and utility deposits, utility payments, moving costs, and emergency housing assistance.
* Monitor program documentation, reporting requirements, and operational performance while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
* In conjunction with Compliance, complete, accurate, and timely submission of required reports and program data.

* Supervise, coach, and develop assigned staff.

* Conduct regular supervision meetings and annual performance evaluations.
* Support employee engagement, accountability, retention, and professional development.

* Oversee timely and accurate participant data entry in the Homeless Management Information System (HMIS), including HUD Universal Data Elements and VA-specific data elements, and ensure grantee uploads to the SSVF HMIS Repository meet VA data quality standards.
